reasoning:
**What is asked.** The highest intraday VIX value (the Cboe daily HIGH) from Monday 23 November to Friday 4 December 2026: nine sessions, with Thanksgiving closed and a half day on 27 November.

**Starting point.** The VIX closed at 35.89 on Friday 20 November after trading as high as 40.03, with the S&P 500 down 3.7% on the day and 8.6% on the week. The window's peak cannot be lower than Monday's own high.

**What changed since my forecast of 22 November.** The weekend brought relief, not more selling. On Sunday evening S&P 500 futures were up 1.9% to 2.1% and Nasdaq-100 futures 2.6% to 2.9% (Bloomberg at 9:07 a.m. Tokyo on 23 November; Fortune, 22 November, 7:13 p.m. ET). Treasury Secretary Bessent said on Sunday that the Fed risks a policy mistake if it overtightens, and traders pared bets on a December hike. If the bounce holds, the VIX starts Monday near 32 to 33, not above Friday's close as I had assumed. It can still fade before New York opens: the Kospi opened 2.6% lower and Euro Stoxx 50 futures are down 2.8%.

**How I get the range.** After past spikes that were followed by a rebound, the two-week peak stayed near the first day's high about half the time (December 2018, August 2024) and ran well above the spike close in the rest (May 2010, March 2020, October 2025). I put the median a little above Friday's close, 3.5 points lower than before, and keep a long upper tail.

**Inside the window.** Core PCE on 25 November, OPEC+ on 29 November, the jobs report on 4 December, the SEC inquiry into Nvidia's accounts, and Iran, where President Trump leans toward strikes after the New Year if there is no deal (Newsquawk, 22 November).

**What would give the other outcomes.** A peak under 33 needs the rebound to hold from Monday's first prints for two weeks. A peak above 50, which I put near 12%, needs a second wave of forced selling.

**Forecast.** Median 37.0; middle half 34.4 to 43.5; 5th to 95th percentile 32.2 to 58.5.
